newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Maju said buyer of Berjaya Singer stake.
newsitem.headline: Maju said buyer of Berjaya Singer stake.

text.p: Malaysian steel concern Maju Holdings Sdn Bhd is buying an 80 percent stake in appliance maker Berjaya Singer Bhd, an industry source close to the deal said on Monday.
"Maju is the buyer for Berjaya Singer shares," the source said. "The deal is for cash," he added. A spokesman for Maju Holdings attending the dedication of a steel mill here declined comment.
The Maju spokesman added that the company will be making an announcement soon but declined to elaborate.
Earlier this month, conglomerate Berjaya Group Bhd said it planned to sell an 80 percent stake in its subsidiary Berjaya Singer.
The sale at a value of 1.196 billion ringgit would result in an exceptional gain of 417.1 million ringgit for the Berjaya Group, a statement from the company had said.

In the statement, Berjaya Group had only described the acquirer as a "third party". The deal was conditioned on Berjaya Group being able to buy back all of Berjaya Singer's subsidiary companies for around 1.317 billion ringgit.
Berjaya Group had said that the buyer of Berjaya Singer would be left with a shell company into which assets would have to be injected "to ensure the future income stream of the company".

Maju Holdings, an unlisted firm, is leading the rescue of loss-making, state-controlled Perwaja Steel Sdn Bhd. An analyst said that Maju could be acquiring Berjaya Singer in order to use it as a shell company to inject Perwaja's assets.

An industry source said another possible scenario was that Berjaya Singer would be injected into engineering firm Kai Peng Bhd and then combined with Perwaja. Maju Holdings is one of two key shareholders of Kai Peng.
Berjaya Singer's stock remained suspended after closing at 5.10 ringgit on April 23.
Shares of Berjaya Group were up two cents to 3.42 ringgit at the close of trading on Monday.
